pages.summary: A triangulation as an object to query: its points, its triangles (or tetrahedra), and what joins what.
body: Made from a connectivity list (a row of point indices for each triangle or tetrahedron) and the points, or from a polyshape (triangulated within its edges). Its properties are `Points` and `ConnectivityList`; it answers `pointLocation`, `nearestNeighbor`, `edges`, `neighbors`, `vertexAttachments`, `edgeAttachments`, `isConnected`, `freeBoundary`, `circumcenter`, `incenter`, the barycentric conversions and, for surfaces, `faceNormal`, `vertexNormal` and `featureEdges`; `triplot`, `trimesh` and `trisurf` draw it.

examples.title: Two triangles of a square
examples.output:
TR = 

  triangulation with properties:

              Points: [4×2 double]
    ConnectivityList: [2×3 double]

ans =

     2     3

pages.summary: The triangle holding each point, and the vertex nearest each point.
body: `pointLocation` gives the ID of the triangle (or tetrahedron) holding each query point, NaN outside, and the barycentric coordinates there. `nearestNeighbor` gives the nearest vertex and the distance; for an alpha shape too.
syntax: The holding simplex and barycentric coordinates.
The nearest vertex and the distance.

examples.title: Points in and out of a square

pages.summary: What joins what in a triangulation: its edges, the triangles at each vertex and each edge, whether vertices are joined, and its boundary.
body: `edges` gives a sorted row `[i j]` for each edge; `vertexAttachments` the triangles at each vertex (counterclockwise in 2-D) and `edgeAttachments` those sharing each edge, as cells; `isConnected` whether two vertices share an edge; `freeBoundary` the edges (facets) used by one triangle only, chained into loops round the region.

examples.title: A square of two triangles
examples.code:
TR = triangulation([1 2 3; 1 3 4], [0 0; 1 0; 1 1; 0 1]);
edges(TR)
vertexAttachments(TR, 1)
edgeAttachments(TR, 1, 3)
[isConnected(TR, 1, 3) isConnected(TR, 2, 4)]
freeBoundary(TR)

pages.summary: Points from barycentric coordinates in simplices, and back.
body: The barycentric coordinates of a point in a triangle are the weights of the three vertices that give the point; they sum to 1 and are all nonnegative inside. Row k uses simplex `ID(k)`.

pages.summary: Normals of a triangulated surface in 3-D, at its triangles and at its vertices, and its sharp edges.
body: `faceNormal` gives the unit normal of each triangle, by the right-hand rule round its vertices; `vertexNormal` the normalized sum of the normals of the triangles at each vertex; `featureEdges` the edges where the two triangles' normals differ by more than an angle (and the boundary's).

examples.title: A folded sheet

pages.summary: The Delaunay triangulation of points as an object: queried like a triangulation, with its convex hull and Voronoi diagram.
body: Duplicate points are removed (with a warning); triangles run counterclockwise in 2-D, and setting `DT.Points` triangulates again. `convexHull` gives the hull as a closed loop of point indices (and the area); `voronoiDiagram` the Voronoi vertices and each point's region. Constrained edges are not supported here, so `isInterior` reports that.
syntax: In 2-D (or `x, y, z`, or a matrix of points).
The hull and its area or volume.

examples.title: A triangulation, its hull, and a point added

pages.summary: Polygons in the plane, with holes and several regions; and regular polygons.
body: `polyshape(x, y)` makes a polygon from its vertices; boundaries are parted by NaN or given in cells, and a boundary inside another is a hole. Crossings and repeated vertices are mended (with a warning) unless `'Simplify', false`. Its properties are `Vertices`, `NumRegions` and `NumHoles`; it answers questions (`area`, `perimeter`, `centroid`, `isinterior`, ...) and is changed by functions that give new polyshapes (`union`, `subtract`, `scale`, `polybuffer`, ...); `plot` draws it filled. `nsidedpoly(n)` is a regular polygon, its vertices on a circle of radius 1 unless given.

pages.summary: A polyshape's measures and parts; and a boundary round points.
body: `centroid` gives the centre of area (of one boundary taken as solid, with I); `perimeter` the length of all boundaries (also of an alpha shape); `boundingbox` the x and y limits; `boundary(pgon)` the boundaries' vertices closed, NaN between. `numboundaries` counts boundaries and `numsides` sides; `ishole` says which boundaries are holes; `issimplified` whether the shape is well defined. Given points, `boundary(x, y, s)` draws a boundary round them, from the convex hull (s = 0) to the tightest single region (s = 1).

examples.title: The square with a hole, measured
examples.code:
p = polyshape({[0 4 4 0], [1 1 3 3]}, {[0 0 4 4], [1 3 3 1]});
[x, y] = centroid(p)
perimeter(p)
[xl, yl] = boundingbox(p)
[numboundaries(p) numsides(p)]
ishole(p)'

y =

ans =

ans =

pages.summary: Whether points are in a polyshape, its vertex nearest each point, and whether polyshapes overlap.
body: `isinterior` is true inside or on the boundary (`on` only on it), and gives the region holding each point. `nearestvertex` gives the nearest vertex's index in `Vertices`, its boundary and its index there. `overlaps` is true when two shapes meet, edges touching included; for an array, a matrix of every pair.
syntax: Inside, on the boundary, and the region.

pages.summary: A polyshape's regions and holes as polyshapes of their own; and boundaries, holes and slivers added or removed.
body: `regions` gives each region (with its holes) as a polyshape, `holes` each hole as a solid polyshape. `addboundary` adds boundaries (one inside the shape becomes a hole), `rmboundary` removes boundaries by number, `rmholes` all holes; `rmslivers` takes off spikes and slits narrower than a tolerance.

examples.title: Two regions, one with a hole

pages.summary: A polyshape scaled, moved, and its boundaries or regions put in order.
body: `scale` multiplies the coordinates by a factor (or `[sx sy]`) about a reference point (the origin unless given); `translate` moves by a vector. `sortboundaries` and `sortregions` order boundaries or regions by `'area'` (the default), `'perimeter'`, `'numsides'` or `'centroid'` (its distance from the origin), `'ascend'` or `'descend'`.

examples.title: A triangle moved, doubled, and regions ordered by size

body: The part of the first not covered by the second; element by element for arrays of the same size, or one polyshape against each of an array. `union`, `intersect` and `xor` combine polyshapes the other ways.

pages.summary: The region within a distance of a polyshape, of points, or of a line.
body: Outward by d (inward for a negative d); corners are rounded unless `'JointType'` is `'square'` or `'miter'` (sharp up to `'MiterLimit'` times d).

pages.summary: An alpha shape: a region round points that can be concave and have holes, tighter as alpha shrinks.
body: The shape is the Delaunay triangles (tetrahedra in 3-D) whose circumradius is at most `Alpha`; with no alpha given, the smallest that takes in every point. `alphaSpectrum` gives the alphas at which the shape changes and `criticalAlpha` the smallest that takes in every point or makes one region. The shape answers `area`, `perimeter` (in 2-D), `volume` and `surfaceArea` (in 3-D), `numRegions`, `inShape`, `nearestNeighbor`, `boundaryFacets` (its boundary) and `alphaTriangulation` (its triangles), and `plot` draws it.
